notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Guard division by zero before computing averages: For weighted-average functions, compute the denominator first and return the zero constant when it is zero to avoid ZeroDivisionError.
  Sum quantities (or weights) up front; if the total is 0, return ZERO immediately. This handles empty invoices and zero-quantity lines without special-casing each line.
- [rb-0006] Read tests and sibling modules before implementing: Exploring the target file, its models, error types, and the provided tests first let the implementation match expected signatures and conventions on the first try.
  Before writing code, cat the target module, related models/money/errors modules, and any test file for the function. Then run the full test suite plus a manual edge-case script (zero, negative, float, bool, wrong state) to confirm behavior before submitting.
- [rb-0001] Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic: When implementing monetary calculations, use the project's existing money utilities (to_money, round_money, ZERO) instead of raw Decimal operations.
  Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling functions like line_total/invoice_total to learn the rounding and coercion conventions. Wrap unit_price with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round the final result with round_money to stay consistent with the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0003] Read the target test and models before implementing: Before writing a new function, inspect the existing test file and dataclass models to confirm signatures, field names, and expected return types.
  Cat tests/test_<feature>.py and ledgerly/models.py to learn exact field names (e.g., line.quantity, line.unit_price) and expected equality semantics (e.g., Decimal == int). This avoids mismatched attribute names and type annotations.
- [rb-0004] Reuse existing money/error helpers for validation: When implementing a billing function, delegate normalization and error signaling to the module's existing helpers rather than reimplementing them.
  Use the repo's `to_money`/`ZERO`/`round_money` helpers to normalize amounts and compare against zero, and raise the project's `BillingError(code, message)` with short machine-readable codes. This matches existing conventions and keeps error codes consistent with hidden tests.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool when validating integer inputs: Python's `bool` is a subclass of `int`, so `isinstance(x, int)` accepts `True`/`False`; explicitly reject bools for integer-only parameters.
  For positive-integer validation write `isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int) or quantity <= 0`. This catches floats, strings, and booleans that would otherwise slip through or be silently coerced.

item.title: Reuse existing time/error helpers for datetime logic
item.description: Before implementing date arithmetic, grep the codebase for existing utilities like ensure_utc and BillingError and reuse them for consistency.
item.content: Search for sibling modules (e.g. subscriptions.py, clock.py, errors.py) that already do similar period math. Reusing ensure_utc for tz normalization and BillingError for validation keeps behavior consistent and satisfies hidden tests expecting those error codes.

item.title: Validate numeric fields defensively before arithmetic
item.description: Guard against bool, non-int, and non-positive period values before using them in timedelta math.
item.content: Check `isinstance(x, bool)` first (bool is an int subclass), then `isinstance(x, int)`, then `x <= 0`, raising the project's domain error. This prevents silent wrong results or TypeError from timedelta.

item.title: Use floor-division formula for strictly-after recurrence
item.description: Compute the first occurrence strictly after a timestamp with `n = (after - start) // length + 1`, handling the before-start case separately.
item.content: For events at start + k*length (k>=1), the strictly-after answer is `start + ((after - start) // length + 1) * length`. If `after < start`, return `start + length` directly. Verify boundary cases (after == start, after == a renewal) with a quick script.
